Subject: Renewal & expansion: term alignment + staged onramp proposal

Hi Chloe,

Thanks for the walkthrough last week. We're ready to start formalizing a renewal + expansion that covers the next product rollout and spikes during Q4. A few constraints from my side:

- We want predictable unit economics across a 24-month horizon, but need burst capacity for months 2–4 of the rollout (estimated +30% peak).
- Procurement prefers one amendment to avoid multiple PO cycles; legal prefers co-terming to our existing agreement where possible.
- We're open to prepay options if it lowers per-token price, but need a clear true-up mechanism for usage variance.

I've attached a short RFP with expected consumption profiles and our preferred co-term date (2027-03-31). Can you share a few concrete term/structure options (pricing delta, billing cadence, and impact on committed capacity) we can circulate with procurement and legal?

Would love to lock a 30-minute call next week.

Thanks,
Jenna

AtlasCloud

Jenna — thanks for the clear brief and the RFP. Below are three pragmatic structures we see working for AtlasCloud; I'll summarize pricing posture and ops impact for each so procurement can compare apples-to-apples.

Option A — 24-month prepay (lowest unit price)
- Commit: 24 months, annualized prepay on year 1 (50%) + year 2 (50%) or single prepay
- Billing: prepay invoice(s) at kickoff
- Burst handling: included as burst credits (first 3 months covered up to +40%)
- Pros/cons: best unit economics, less flexible on true-up (we offer a 10% true-up band)

Option B — 18-month staged bands (recommended middle ground)
- Commit: 18 months, 3 bands (base / growth / peak) with automatic staged unlocks aligned to rollout months
- Billing: quarterly invoicing with true-up at 6/12/18 months
- Burst handling: temporary burst pool + one-time onramp credit applied in month 2
- Pros/cons: balances flexibility and price; easier operational reconciliation

Option C — 12 + 12 (annual review, co-terming enabled)
- Commit: initial 12-month firm commitment + optional 12-month rollover with pre-agreed uplift bands
- Billing: standard monthly/quarterly; true-up at year end
- Burst handling: pay-as-you-go for overage with capped uplift
- Pros/cons: maximum contractual flexibility, higher unit price when compared to A/B

Next steps I suggest: 1) Confirm whether AtlasCloud prefers prepay or staged billing; 2) If legal requires co-terming to 2027-03-31, we'll draft amendment language that keeps billing cadence intact but aligns contract end-dates; 3) If you like Option B, Rishi and I will draft an amendment + one-page pricing summary for procurement.

Meeting: I'm available Wed/Thu AM PT — sending a calendar invite if that works.

Best,
Chloe Martin
Account Executive, Renewals & Expansion
Redwood Inference

All — quick internal note and suggested path forward copied into the thread so procurement/legal see our working assumptions.

Summary of recommended commercial: go with Option B (18-month staged bands) with the following guardrails:
- Start date: effective on signature; co-term to AtlasCloud's preferred 2027-03-31 by prorating months to equal the 18-month economic exposure.
- Pricing bands: define three discrete bands with per-token rates and a pre-agreed escalation if sustained usage breaches the top band >60 days.
- Onramp credits: apply a one-time credit equal to 12% of month-1 estimated spend to offset initial integration friction.
- Billing & true-up: quarterly invoices; true-ups at Q2/Q4 and contract close.

Operational notes for Chloë/CS: we'll need minimum lead time for burst capacity (7 business days) unless we provision a reserved burst pool (adds ~5% to committed spend). Recommend offering the reserved burst pool to AtlasCloud for predictability; it smooths ops and reduces last-minute allocation requests. Lauren, can you confirm margin impact on the reserved pool?

Attached is a draft amendment with language for co-terming and staged unlocks — it's intentionally lean to speed procurement. If Jenna's team accepts the approach, we can route this to legal and procurement as our recommended commercial path.

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
